top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) rest on a distinct invention, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, that the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 single-quantum-system prize did not cover. The performance at the 10^-18 level has been reproduced by independent groups (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) with different species. The two-name allocation is clean, and the Ye 2005 overlap objection was removed once it was established that Ye was not a laureate. I accept that the fundamental-physics output so far consists of limits and demonstrations, so the citation should stay on the instrument. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a respectable second, with real conceptual novelty, but its three-name credit leaves a visible gap (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, and the 3D work) that I cannot adjudicate from my own field, so I rank it below P001. Some award is better than none, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: No apparent connection to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp from my profile. As WACQT director and a superconducting-circuit theorist at Chalmers I would recuse on circuit QED (B006), which is not in this slate.
